key_insight: AutoPass improves compiler performance tuning by letting LLM agents use compiler-internal and runtime evidence to iteratively choose better optimization settings instead of guessing from a black-box compiler.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical, training-free way to automate compiler optimization across new benchmarks and hardware targets with minimal manual retuning.
method: Multi-agent LLM framework for compiler performance tuning
Queries LLVM internal optimization states and intermediate representation
Uses runtime feedback to diagnose regressions and refine optimization configurations iteratively
evidence_signal: Evaluated on LLVM for server-grade x86-64 and embedded ARM64, AutoPass achieved geometric-mean speedups of 1.043x and 1.117x over LLVM -O3.
watch_item: Results depend on noisy runtime measurements and compiler-internal signals, so stability and generalization may vary across workloads and platforms.
paper_title: AutoPass: Evidence-Guided LLM Agents for Compiler Performance Tuning
